notes: ICP system. Styles 1-3 are identical to Tempstar styles 1-3 in example serials, shapes, and positions. NOT usesStylesOf Tempstar because Tempstar lists an additional style 6 that the Keeprite page does not list; verbatim reuse would add an unverified style to Keeprite. Styles 4-5 are chart-verified and shipped (image-pass Nov 8): style 4 from the 8-digit chart (dual-candidate years), style 5 from the year-letter chart; same tail caveat as Tempstar (see style notes). Keeprite's charts are identical in content to Tempstar's.

styles.notes: Year is 2nd-3rd digits, week is 4th-5th digits. Week decode for the example is 16.

styles.era: Letter followed by 9 digits, with printed MFG date on tag
styles.notes: Page states this serial is identical in system to style 1; the printed MFG date 2/92 corroborates year 1992 and week 06. Pattern and positions duplicate style 1, so this style never wins first-match, but its decode is identical.

styles.era: 10-character format, year-week in first four digits
styles.notes: Year is 1st-2nd digits, week is 3rd-4th digits. Week decode for the example is 14.

Chart-verified (image-pass Nov 8): year is the 1st digit, week is the 2nd-3rd digits. The chart itself states the unit was manufactured in the 5th week of either 1983/1993, so the year is an explicit dual candidate, not a guess. Era 1980-1993 is chart-stated. Keeprite's chart is identical in content to Tempstar's.

Chart-verified (image-pass Nov 8): year is the 3rd character. The page shows only the placeholder sample Z3Z xxxxx, used here as the example (the page's own placeholder, not an invented serial). The 5-character tail is shown only as undifferentiated XXXXX on the chart; the pattern uses [A-Z0-9]{5} because no tail shape is evidenced (digit-only would be an unevidenced narrowing). Year letters skip I. Era 1970-1994 is chart-stated. Keeprite's chart is identical in content to Tempstar's.
